body:
Distilled from a heavy real-use field report. Two conventions to bless in SKILL.md/README, and a non-goals section to protect against future scope creep.

CONVENTIONS TO DOCUMENT:
1. Relationships beyond deps via a parseable note prefix. T-40/T-45 already rejected adding a schema-level relation field in favor of the note convention; the field report confirms that call and only asks that the convention be documented with a parseable prefix (e.g. note "relates: T-3", "split-of: T-53", "dup-of: T-9") so it composes/greps. Do NOT add a schema field — keep it a documented note convention.
2. Priority x labels as orthogonal axes. priority is a flat int; labels are an orthogonal axis. An agent-vs-human label used as a "safe to do autonomously / needs a human decision" axis, cross-producted with priority, was genuinely useful for triage. `list -l agent --sort=priority` already supports it. Recommend it as a convention.

NON-GOALS TO PRESERVE (do not "improve" into Jira):
- Notes-as-audit-trail is the killer feature (pinning why/what-was-verified survives compaction and hand-offs).
- Repo-local, zero-infra, travels with git.
- States + labels are exactly enough; resist workflow ceremony.
- Multi-writer path is load-bearing in real use (Claude + Codex + Copilot + 2 humans concurrently): treat optimistic locking, the actor field, and ref stamping as first-class invariants when changing event handling.
title: document agent-oriented conventions and design non-goals (field report)
